title: Prove a sharp entropy threshold for adaptive tail gates (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped written proof with exact finite corroboration. The adaptive compiler's tail/ordering gates have a sharp entropy screen, exact for a two-rank target:

```text
q=T(t)/P(t)>=1, 0<x<p<1
p = target tilted mean of normalized log rank
x = paid tilted mean in the same normalization

two target ranks: gates feasible iff log q < D(x||p)
D(x||p)=x log(x/p)+(1-x)log((1-x)/(1-p))
```

For general finite target profiles this is a sharp sufficient test from range and mean. At equality, positive mass at an interior target rank still gives a strict passing point; a two-rank profile fails. PROOF.md covers the remaining mean/range regimes.

The exact new integer fixture `W_4=1,W_256=32,P_16=c,t=1/2`, with `1<=c<=128`, passes precisely when `c>=7`. Its optimized scalar numerator is exactly 24. At c=7, `a=1,b=31,M=2^132,s=1/2,lambda=3/2` gives `u=2049/2056<1`, `v=64*(6/7)^32<1`, and the required forward ordering.

Dillon Amburgey's [#4532](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4532) retains credit for the exact scalar gate equivalence used as a cited premise. The new contribution is the closed-form screen, strict equality case and histogram transition, rather than a replay of that predecessor. Exponential convexity and binary entropy are classical methods; global literature priority for them is unclaimed. Credit zxv #4436/#4483, Jacob Alan Sussman's compiler, Ryanson Jonathan #4459 and the retained native/helper/geometry/outer lineage. Produced by Nick Petalas. Apache-2.0.

## Evidence

Before, the cited scalar criterion asks whether some positive lambda satisfies `T(t-lambda) exp(lambda mu_P)<P(t)`. After, the two-rank case is a closed-form strict entropy comparison with an exact equality classification.

Local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass:

- All 8,439 histogram cases in the declared q>=1 domain agree between the entropy and separate monomial critical-value classifiers. All 5,444 passing cases have a literal rational passing point; 2,995 fail, with 14,975 literal failing-point controls.
- All 288 three-position laws satisfy the chord bound, with 256 strict interior cases and 32 endpoint equalities. All 128 fixture integers, the original three gates at the rational witness, eleven controls and three corrupted verifier copies behave as required.
- Warning-strict direct normal/optimized runs take 0.115s each in the observed local runs. The full registered replay takes 0.454s; each registered command is comfortably below five minutes. These are local budget observations, not performance guarantees.
- Metadata/pins, AST/function bounds, exact committed bytes and source-history preflight pass for all six package files at `f7c2625f5488b09e6d19b4bed7efe8b4e89a6782`.
- Official export integrity and optimized read-only Git-free replay pass. All seven exported files, including the export manifest, remain unchanged. Normal, optimized and exported checks produce generated source-bound receipt `c53cbd91601cc5528224d14bab34a26401f2911db4844603f3d87fb5d1364ef7`.

From the repository root:

```sh

/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/adaptive-tail-entropy/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/adaptive-tail-entropy
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/adaptive-tail-entropy --check-source-history
```

Any CPython 3.12 executable may replace the absolute local interpreter path. Standard library only. Expected markers include `PASS_ADAPTIVE_TAIL_ENTROPY`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The universal claim rests on the written proof and cited scalar equivalence; finite replay corroborates its declared domains.

## Limitations and claim correction

The [advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19147083) incorrectly predicted mirror slack for the histogram fixture. The [progress correction](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19147154) explicitly reports that its source/exit windows are disjoint. The delivered result covers tail and ordering feasibility only, and the verifier records mirror failure. No full compiler admission follows.

These are abstract histograms. Native realizability, full mirror/recurrence funding, chronological widths, owned restoration, adapters, precision, movement, stock and outer transfer remain separate obligations. Failure of the sufficient entropy screen is inconclusive for general target profiles. No physical supplier, complete multiplication theorem, new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed. No native, selected scientific cold replay, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. All registered obligations ran locally.

## Open next questions

1. Apply the screen to one actual changed native profile with pinned target/paid histograms and complete mirror cells. Native semantics, width, funding and the physical bill remain blockers.
2. Bound the strict chord deficit from a specified positive interior mass to improve the screen above the endpoint threshold. The present proof supplies only a qualitative equality improvement.

No further research extension is included.

## Related open work

- [#5243](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5243) screens a hypothetical changed p16/a7 paid profile at a fixed conditional compiler point. This contribution derives an analytic tail/ordering criterion for arbitrary finite profiles and an abstract integer fixture; it does not compute or compare that PR's kappa or establish its missing physical pair.
- The live open-PR/topic searches and latest handoff refresh found no open PR studying this entropy threshold or the same fixture transition. Sparse notes, arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain coverage limits. The merged #4532/#4483 predecessors are credited above.
